_comment: The governance watchdogs run from this roster, as cron runs on this
profile. Unlike upstream, this roster is NOT inert: the gateway's own
ticker only ever ticks the Chat Agent's store, but that store carries
`profile-cron-tick`, which runs `hermes cron tick` against every named
profile with work due (see 'What fires the schedule' in
docs/site/src/content/docs/concepts/autonomous-watchdogs.md). An enabled
entry here therefore fires in its own process, with this profile's
persona, toolsets, `skills`, `model` and `max_turns`.
Do not add any of these ids to agents/chat/defaults/cron/jobs.json as
well. Two rosters both carrying one is that audit running twice per
schedule, concurrently with itself, writing its ledger issue twice.
The trailing `enabled: false` entries are tombstones — ids an earlier
release shipped and this one has retired. They are kept because
profile_scaffold.merge_cron_store adds and overwrites but never prunes,
so deleting an entry only ends this image's ability to hold it off: the
volume's copy goes on firing. Shipping it disabled is what stops it, and
an id is safe to delete only once every live volume has merged that
disabled form. (`retire_cron_jobs` is the escape hatch for the case that
cannot cover — an id that has to stop firing in one release — and the
entrypoint names those ids explicitly.)
Hermes ignores every top-level key but `jobs` when it loads the store,
so this note is inert.

jobs.name: Security & RBAC Posture Audit
jobs.prompt: Run the daily fleet security and RBAC posture audit. Read the SOP at 'governance/compliance_audit_sop.md' in your profile home — all 406 lines of it, before you run anything. Its eleven checks are section 2, lines 102-314, so a read that stops early skips almost the entire audit and reports a clean fleet it never looked at. Then execute it exactly, using the fleet-audit skill to open and close the audit run.

jobs.name: Workload Reliability Audit
jobs.prompt: Run the daily workload reliability audit. Read the SOP at 'governance/obtainability_audit_sop.md' in your profile home — all 282 lines of it, before you run anything. Its eleven checks are section 3, lines 86-215, so a read that stops early skips almost the entire audit and reports a clean fleet it never looked at. Then execute it exactly, using the fleet-audit skill to open and close the audit run.

jobs.name: Upgrade & Patch Readiness Audit
jobs.prompt: Run the weekly GKE upgrade and patch readiness audit. Read the SOP at 'governance/security_patch_orchestrator_sop.md' in your profile home — all 283 lines of it, before you run anything. Its ten checks are section 3, lines 114-218, so a read that stops early skips almost the entire audit and reports a clean fleet it never looked at. Then execute it exactly, using the fleet-audit skill to open and close the audit run. This audit is read-only: never upgrade a cluster.

jobs.name: Fleet Waste Audit
jobs.prompt: Run the weekly fleet waste audit. Read the SOP at 'governance/fleet_wide_cost_analysis_sop.md' in your profile home — all 261 lines of it, before you run anything. Its ten checks are section 3, lines 87-193, so a read that stops early skips almost the entire audit and reports a clean fleet it never looked at. Then execute it exactly, using the fleet-audit skill to open and close the audit run. Report findings in resource units only — you have no pricing data.

jobs.name: Fleet Consistency Drift Audit
jobs.prompt: Run the weekly fleet consistency drift audit. Read the SOP at 'governance/fleet_consistency_drift_sop.md' in your profile home — all 264 lines of it, before you run anything. Its nineteen facets are section 4, lines 90-195, so a read that stops early skips almost the entire audit and reports a clean fleet it never looked at. Then execute it exactly, using the fleet-audit skill to open and close the audit run. The baseline is derived from the live fleet itself — never from an external blueprint.

jobs.name: AI Workload Security Audit
jobs.prompt: Run the daily AI workload security audit. Read the SOP at 'governance/ai_security_audit_sop.md' in your profile home — all 314 lines of it, before you run anything. Its six checks are section 3, lines 128-245, so a read that stops early skips almost the entire audit and reports a clean fleet it never looked at. Section 2 defines which workloads count as AI workloads; on a cluster running none the six checks still ran and matched nothing, so record all six in checks_run with the collection command — never leave checks_run empty, which the validator rejects. Then execute it exactly, using the fleet-audit skill to open and close the audit run.

jobs.name: GitHub Issue Resolver
jobs.prompt: Run the github-issue-resolver skill to poll, triage, investigate, and resolve unaddressed open issues on our target repository strictly according to the skill's safety red lines, scope constraints, and turn completion checklist.

jobs.name: Blueprint Sync
jobs.prompt: Execute GKE blueprint alignment audit. Read 'governance/blueprint_sync_sop.md' in your profile home and perform the daily GKE cluster compliance checks against the master blueprints.

jobs.name: Policy Propagation
jobs.prompt: Propagate updated operational policies. Read 'governance/policy_propagation_sop.md' in your profile home and inspect the latest security policies and resource configs across all clusters directly.

jobs.name: Global Capacity Orchestrator
jobs.prompt: Execute cross-cluster capacity optimization. Read 'governance/global_capacity_orchestrator_sop.md' in your profile home to analyze fleet-wide regional demand and inspect cluster capacity pools directly.

jobs.name: Standardization Validator
jobs.prompt: Run weekly structural GKE alignment audit. Read 'governance/standardization_validator_sop.md' in your profile home to perform deep-diff analysis between GKE live states and global standards.

jobs.name: Lifecycle / Deprecation Manager
jobs.prompt: Execute monthly toolchain lifecycle audit. Read 'governance/lifecycle_deprecation_manager_sop.md' in your profile home to track K8s version deprecations and proactively notify development teams.
